description: Agent Onboarding: submit every system and tool a new agent’s job needs or the agent can reach: optionally the agent with its id, when it runs its first task and where it runs its job (production, staging or a sandbox); each system with its id, name, kind (an API, a database, a tool, an inbox, a dashboard, a wallet, a file store or other), whether the written job needs it, whether the agent’s access is set up, for a system the job does not need whether access was removed or never granted, how access was tested (a real task run end to end, a connection only, or not tested), what the test showed (passed, failed or partly worked), where and when it was tested; and optionally the days before the first task after which a test counts as stale (14 when left out). The signed report gives every system with its test’s age in days and its status as proven, not_provisioned, failed, partial, elsewhere, stale, late, connection_only, untested, closed, open or unknown, and counts the systems, those needed, proven, broken and untested and those not needed and still open, and names broken access: a system the job needs with no access set up, and a failed test; then a test that only partly worked, one run only in another environment, one run too long before the first task or after it, and a system the job does not need left open, with the fix for each. A test of the connection only, no end-to-end test, and an unstated need, set-up, start, environment or test date leave the access untested. This reads the systems one new agent needs, provisioned and proven before its first task: which endpoints agents can call that delete, administer or move money is wever_tool-exposure-check, what a read-only agent can change is wever_read-only-scope-check, paths from a test environment into production systems are wever_sandbox-isolation-check and the rules a gateway enforces are wever_gateway-rules-check. Verdict onboarding_access_broken, onboarding_access_partial, onboarding_access_untested or onboarding_access_proven. POST /api/onboarding-access-check. Reads only the recorded onboarding material in the call: no network request, fetch, money movement, message, configuration change or external write; no credential is issued, rotated or revoked, no permission granted or removed, no wallet funded or moved, no limit set and the agent is not approved, and a credential found in supplied text is named by kind and never repeated. Agent Onboarding reads the setup of a new agent joining a system, before its first task: whether its identity is established and tied to its owner, whether its credentials are scoped to its job, stored where they belong and kept out of prompts, logs and shared documents, whether its wallet is the right one, funded only to the job with recovery recorded by the owner before funds move, whether its permissions match the written job, whether its limits sit in code with a human handoff, whether the systems it needs are provisioned and tested, whether it is ready for its first task and whether the onboarding record matches what is live. It is not vetting an outside party (wever_counterparty-onboarding-check reads a counterparty’s onboarding packet before the system transacts with it; an onboarding check reads an agent joining the system itself), not a grant or an authority for one action (wever_consent-scope-check reads whether a principal’s grant covers a use and wever_authority-scope-check whether an actor’s access fits its grant for an action; an onboarding check reads that the grant and the authority were put in place before the first task, and does not re-check them per action), not a limit in flight (the wever_limit checks and wever_agent-budget-guard read limits for work already running; an onboarding check reads that limits were set in code before it starts) and not an action’s consequences (the wever_risk checks read one planned action; an onboarding check reads readiness to start). Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-onboarding-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-onboarding/.

environment.description: Where the agent runs its job: production, staging or a sandbox.

starts_at.description: When the agent runs its first task.

label.description: Optional name recorded in the report.

stale_days.description: Days before the first task after which a test counts as stale; 14 when left out.

systems.description: Every system and tool the job needs or the agent can reach.

closed.description: For a system the job does not need: access was removed or never granted.

id.description: The system id, such as s1.

kind.description: An API, a database, a tool, an inbox, a dashboard, a wallet, a file store or other.

name.description: The system or tool, such as the order API.

provisioned.description: The agent’s access to it is set up.

result.description: What the test showed: passed, failed or partly worked.

tested.description: How access was tested: a real task run end to end, a connection only, or not tested.

name: wever_onboarding-access-check
title: Onboarding access check
